results.hypothesis: To evaluate whether survival models incorporating time-dependent variables and dynamic prediction mechanisms perform better than binary classifiers in predicting readmission outcomes when follow-up windows vary significantly, as measured by Brier score and time-dependent AUC.
results.author: coder-agent
results.baseline: Performance of binary classifiers (Logistic Regression, XGBoost with binary objective) trained on static features without time-dependent variables or dynamic updates.
results.success_criteria: If survival models with time-dependent variables and dynamic prediction achieve lower Brier scores and higher time-dependent AUC values compared to binary classifiers, the hypothesis is supported. If not, the hypothesis is refuted.
results.notes: Only binary classifiers were successfully trained and evaluated.
